status_reviews.summary: Status=operating remains correct. Estonia halted Russian gas imports in 2022, ending this corridor's EXPORT function, but per BISI's independent 2025-04-18 report the 'Kohtla-Järve-Leningrad connection' (covering this corridor, of which Line II/P5589 is a string) has not carried commercial gas since 2019 -- three years BEFORE the 2022 Estonia embargo, and for reasons unrelated to it -- yet 'remains available for technical gas supply to system operators and pipeline stations.' Per the batch brief's own rule, a pipe that has stopped exporting but remains in the Unified Gas Supply System stays 'operating,' not idle/mothballed/retired; there is no distinct GEM controlled-vocabulary status for 'technically available, commercially unused.' This is a documented distinction (BISI's own language), not a geopolitical inference.
status_reviews.caveat: Note for context, not a status change: commercial use of this connection ceased in 2019, predating the 2022 Estonia Russian-gas import ban by three years, so the 2022 embargo is not itself the cause of this line's idled commercial state. If GEM later adds a distinct 'idle/standby, technically available' status value, this row (and its sibling P2326) would be candidates -- but no such value exists in the current controlled vocabulary, and BISI's own 'remains available' language supports keeping operating.
status_reviews.researcher_notes: This is the identical status-review judgment already staged on sibling row P2326 (Line I) -- the BISI report discusses the Kohtla-Järve-Leningrad connection as a corridor, not line-by-line, so the same evidence and verdict apply to both GEM rows. Cross-checked against Elering's (Estonian TSO) network materials showing Estonia's current primary Russia-interconnection point sits at Izborsk/Pskov, not at this Kohtla-Järve corridor -- consistent with this corridor being a separate, longer-idled connection rather than the active modern import route, and consistent with BISI's 2019 commercial-halt date.
